item.title: ‘The Implications Are Global’: International Music Publishers Welcomes Australian Government’s ‘Landmark’ Statement on AI
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news and trends in the music industry. Today, we're coming to you from Sydney, Australia, where the prime minister has made a significant announcement about copyright protection and AI.
[Short music transition]
Host: In a speech at the University of Sydney, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese made it clear that tech and AI companies cannot use copyright-protected works, including music, without the artist's consent, credit, and compensation. He stated, "No company should use Australian books, music, art, or news to build or train AI without the artist's control. That includes the artist's control of the price and value of their work. Anything less, is theft."
[Short music transition]
Host: This announcement has been warmly welcomed by the international music publishers community, including the International Confederation of Music Publishers, which represents 90% of the world's commercially released music. John Phelan, the director general of ICMP, noted that the implications of this decision are global and that the industry looks forward to building AI and music markets that are based on consent, credit, and compensation.
[Short music transition]
Host: The Australian music industry has been lobbying against any weakening of copyright protections, with organizations like AMPAL and APRA AMCOS calling on the government to reject any changes that could put the country's rich cultural heritage at risk. As Prime Minister Albanese said, "Australia holds something no other country possesses: more than sixty thousand years of First Nations culture. Those songs, stories, images, and languages are living cultural heritage."
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to this episode of our podcast. It's clear that the Australian government is taking a strong stance on copyright protection and AI, and we'll be keeping an eye on how this develops in the coming months. Join us next time for more news and insights from the music industry.
